verdict.rationale: The only relevant evidence is Bridge's orchestration docs. They describe a static template that gives customers persistent deposit instructions they can reuse, which suggests a dedicated deposit route per customer. The docs do not say these instructions are unique per customer, that they are named virtual accounts or deposit addresses, or that incoming funds are tied back to the payer for reconciliation. Missing for 10: explicit per-customer virtual accounts or deposit addresses, documented automatic attribution and reconciliation of who paid, first-party Stripe crypto docs (not just Bridge), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, incoming funds are attributable — named virtual accounts or dedicated deposit addresses per customer so reconciliation knows who paid without manual matching

citations.quote: A static template provides persistent deposit instructions your customers can use repeatedly.
